nations.name: Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe
nations.lands: Cheyenne River Reservation, central South Dakota, United States; headquarters in Eagle Butte

facts.text: The Tribe’s history page traces the reservation’s land base through the Fort Laramie Treaties of 1851 and 1868 and the Sioux Act of 1889.
The Tribe’s TECA Office describes administering grants to eligible Tribal programs and entities, with budgetary and operational oversight.
facts.evidence: We provide budgetary and operational oversight

facts.text: The Tribal Education Agency lists developing infrastructure for Lakota language, culture and standards among its services, alongside school partnerships and technical assistance.
facts.evidence: Develop infrastructure for CRST Lakota Language, culture, and standards

facts.text: The Tribe’s Cultural Preservation Office describes a goal of preserving, strengthening and promoting its way of life for future generations.
facts.evidence: preserve, strengthen, and promote our way of life
